chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdallah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said:

Abu Kurayb al-Azdi and Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi gave witness in the presence of Sharik while he was the judge. He looked at their faces for a long moment and then said: 'Two Ja'faris, two Fatimis!' so they began to cry. He said to them: 'What makes you cry?' They said to him: 'You have attributed us to a group who are not pleased with the likes of us being counted among their fellows because of what they see of the deficiency in our worship, and you have attributed us to a man who is not pleased that the likes of us be associated among his Shia. If he does us a favour and accepts us, then he is the one who bestows favour upon us and excels.' Sharik smiled, then said: 'If there are men, let them be like you. O Walid, permit them this time (and do not return them a second time).' They said: 'We made the pilgrimage and recounted to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the incident, so he said: 'What is with Sharik? May Allah partner him up on the Day of Resurrection with two strips of fire.'

key_terms.جَعْفَرَيَانِ: Two Ja'faris (referring to their attribution to Ja'far ibn Muhammad)
key_terms.شَرَاكَيْنِ: Two strips (referring to the straps of sandals, used as a metaphor for paired reward or burden)
key_terms.فَطِمِيَانِ: Two Fatimis (referring to their attribution to the family of Fatima)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Sharik accepting the testimony of Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Kurayb?
ai.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi recounts an incident where the judge Sharik accepted the testimony of Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn Muslim, noting their humble status despite their attribution to Ja'far al-Sadiq. The Imam later praised this judicial leniency by prophesying that Sharik would be paired with 'two strips of fire' in the afterlife, a metaphor for the reward of his good judgment.
